Put it in a new migration file, `migrations/0008_add_customer_phone.sql`. Don't edit `migrations/0007_add_customers.sql`, even though that's where the `customers` table is created.

This project's memory says files in `migrations/` have already been applied in production, so they must never be edited. New schema changes go in a new file with the next 4-digit number. The latest is `0007`, so yours is `0008`:

```sql
ALTER TABLE customers ADD COLUMN phone TEXT;
```

I left it nullable because existing customer rows have no phone number. If you want `NOT NULL`, you'll need a default value or a backfill step first.

Separately, `0007` names the email column `emial`, a typo. Any code or SQL that touches that column has to use that spelling. If you want it renamed, that would also need its own new migration (e.g. `ALTER TABLE customers RENAME COLUMN emial TO email;`), not an edit to `0007`.
